summary: AgroStake is a comprehensive, offline-first agricultural intelligence system designed to optimize crop planning and soil health for farming operations of any scale. Developed by Team OVERVOLT for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, AgroStake bridges the critical gap between macro-level satellite observations and micro-level ground conditions. The system combines an in-situ 7-in-1 soil stake (measuring moisture, temperature, electrical conductivity, pH, and N-P-K) that transmits data via long-range 900 MHz XBee radio to an internet-connected base receiver, ensuring reliable operation even in remote fields without cellular service. By fusing local ground truth with 20+ years of NASA Earth observations (including NASA POWER, SMAP, IMERG, and MODIS/VIIRS) and modular land-suitability databases (such as UPRA), AgroStake analyzes soil and climate dynamics to deliver three top crop options tailored to the grower's priorities. Beyond local farm optimization, AgroStake creates a vital two-way exchange of value with the scientific community by feeding localized, calibrated soil measurements back into global ecosystems to validate and enhance satellite models worldwide.
details:
AgroStake: Detailed Project Submission Answers

1. What does it do and how does it work?

AgroStake is an offline-first agricultural intelligence system that bridges macro-level satellite observations with micro-level ground conditions. It operates through a robust two-node hardware architecture paired with a Progressive Web App (PWA):

  • Node 1 (The In-Situ Soil Stake): Inserted into the root zone (25 cm depth), it features a 7-in-1 sensor measuring soil moisture, temperature, electrical conductivity (EC), pH, and N-P-K via RS485 (Modbus). Powered by an ESP32 microcontroller, an e-ink screen, and a 6V 2W solar panel, it provides instant readings. For dry conditions, a pre-wetting and guide-hole protocol ensures optimal sensor contact, while multi-point sampling with median filtering filters out stones or air pockets. It features an integrated speaker for voice guidance to support growers with low literacy.
  • Node 2 (The 900 MHz Base Receiver): Since remote fields lack cellular connectivity, the stake transmits telemetry via a long-range Digi XBee-PRO 900HP (S3B) radio (900/915 MHz) to a farmhouse base receiver. The base is powered by an AC-DC Hi-Link HLK-5M05 module, protected by a 1A/250V fuse and MOV 14D241K varistor, with dual 18650 batteries in parallel, a TP4056 Boost module (5.0V), and a 470µF capacitor. Its "Store & Forward" memory caches readings with precise timestamps during power outages and automatically syncs when connectivity returns.
  • The Web Platform & NASA Integration: Accessible at agrostakee-1.onrender.com, the user logs in with their mobile number and password, taps their farm on the map, and the backend queries over 20 years of historical climate and Earth observation data from NASA POWER, SMAP L4, GPM IMERG, MODIS/VIIRS NDVI, and SRTM elevation. Combining this with modular land-suitability zoning (such as UPRA in Colombia or FAO GAEZ globally) and the grower's priorities (water, nitrogen, erosion, market value), the platform generates the top 3 recommended crop options with multi-year outlooks (1, 5, and 10 years).

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Offline-First Resilience: Works seamlessly in remote rural areas without constant internet connection or cellular coverage in the field.
  • Actionable Intelligence: Translates complex lab numbers and raw satellite feeds into simple, clear crop choices and management guidance.
  • Cultural & Accessibility Bridge: Integrates traditional agricultural knowledge (such as lunar calendar cycles) and audio guidance, lowering the barrier to technology adoption.
  • Cost-Effective & Free Access: Eliminates expensive professional soil lab tests ($150k–$400k COP per test) and maintains a 100% free web platform for growers (intentionally omitting SMS password recovery costs).

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

  • Improved Soil Health & Resilience: Replaces destructive monocultures with optimized crop rotations (e.g., nitrogen-fixing legumes followed by heavy feeders and cover crops) to restore organic matter and prevent erosion.
  • Climate Adaptation: Helps farmers adapt to erratic rainfall patterns and extreme weather shifts by utilizing 20 years of NASA historical climate data combined with real-time ground telemetry.
  • Global Scientific Contribution (Two-Way Value Exchange): Feeds localized, lab-calibrated soil measurements back into global ecosystems, providing critical "ground truth" to validate and enhance NASA's satellite models worldwide.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Hardware & Electronics: ESP32 microcontrollers, 7-in-1 RS485 soil sensors (Modbus RTU), Digi XBee-PRO 900HP (S3B) 900 MHz radio modules, e-ink displays, 6V 2W solar panels, Hi-Link HLK-5M05 AC-DC power modules, TP4056 charge/boost modules, 18650 lithium batteries, MOV 14D241K varistors, and 470µF capacitors.
  • Software & Development: Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture, and Render hosting.
  • APIs & Open Data: NASA POWER API, SMAP L4, GPM IMERG, MODIS/VIIRS NDVI, SRTM, and modular adaptors for UPRA and FAO GAEZ databases.

5. In what way is your project creative?

AgroStake's creativity lies in its closed-loop integration and cultural synergy. While satellite monitoring and soil sensors exist separately, AgroStake uniquely combines low-cost local telemetry, long-range 900 MHz radio networking, open NASA datasets, and modular national land-suitability layers into an autonomous decision engine. Furthermore, it treats traditional farmer wisdom (lunar planting cycles and voice assistance) not as a barrier, but as a core design pillar that builds immediate trust and adoption. Finally, it establishes a true two-way data exchange, turning every deployed stake into a calibration node that helps NASA improve global Earth observations.

6. What factors did your team take into consideration?

  • Field Reliability & Environmental Hardening: Accounted for harsh coastal/tropical conditions by planning IP67 enclosures, cable glands, silica gel packets, and tropicalized PCB conformal coating against saline air and humidity.
  • Power and Connectivity Constraints: Designed a dual-node radio topology (XBee 900 MHz) with robust power resilience (AC-DC module + backup 18650 batteries + fuse/MOV protection) to withstand rural power outages and lack of mobile signal.
  • Data Uncertainty & Calibration: Addressed the inherent limitations of low-cost indirect NPK sensors by implementing firmware safeguards (dry soil pre-checks, median filtering of 5–10 readings) and local laboratory calibration campaigns (e.g., AGROSAVIA) to provide transparent confidence indices (Safe data, Approximate data, Repeat reading).
  • Scalability & Modularity: Architected the software with an interchangeable data layer, ensuring the recommendation engine can connect to any nation's official land database or fall back to global FAO GAEZ data seamlessly.
